To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of OLIG2 in the glial component of a gliosarcoma does not exclude the possibility that it is a pure sarcoma and that IDH1 is not expressed in small cell gliobastoma, granular cell GBM, or giant cell GBM.

OLIG2 is expressed in most non-conventional gliomas and can be helpful in distinguishing them from other entities, while IDH1-R 132H is expressed in the vast majority of glioblastoma, with oligodendroglioma component, and can help distinguish it from primary glioblastomas.

OLIG2 expression is retained in the primitive neuroectoderm-like foci of glioblastoma and in the glial component of the majority of gliosarcoma, while the glial component is almost always positive for IDH1 in glioblastoma, but rarely in gliosarcoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the diagnostic utility of IDH1 and OLIG2 in the challenging glioblastomas variants.
the expression of OLIG2, IDH1 and other proteins in glioblastoma and other high-grade gliomas.
the diagnostic and prognostic implications of IDH mutation and expression of OLIG2 in rarer gliobastoma variants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression patterns of these two markers are not sufficiently robust to be of practical use in distinguishing between glioblastoma, glioblastoma variant, and central nervous system PNT.
OLIG2 and/or IDH1 immunoreactivity is present in the majority of glioblastoma cases, and that their presence is useful in the diagnosis of specific variants.
IDH1 is not expressed in any of the small cell gliobastomas, granular glioblastomas and giant cell gliomas that have been studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

IDH1 is expressed in the vast majority of secondary glioblastoma and a minority of primary glioblastomas; OLIG2 is strongly expressed in the majority and variably expressed in the remainder of glioblastoma subtypes; OLIG2 expression in PNET-like fOCI provides a useful diagnostic distinction from CNS PNETs; and OLIG2 is not expressed in pure sarcoma.

the combination of OLIG2 expression in all gliobastomas with an oligodentrogli component, IDH1 in most of these, OLIG2 in most gliosarcomatous components, IDH1 negativity in most glioblastoma subtypes other than glioblastomas and glioblastomas containing an oligodendrogli component, and OLIG2 negativity in pure sarcomatous lesions, would be a helpful diagnostic approach.
OLIG2 expression is a useful marker to support a glioblastoma diagnosis in most cases, but it does not provide a reliable distinction from sarcomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
these markers can be useful in the diagnosis of rare and difficult glioblastoma subtypes, and we recommend their use in the diagnostic workup of these cases.

OLIG2 is a very useful marker to help distinguish glioblastoma from other high-grade gliomas, while IDH1 expression is a helpful marker to distinguish glioblastomas from secondary glioblastoma and primary glioblastomas.
the expression pattern of these two antibodies is highly informative in a wide variety of glioblastoma subtypes.
